summary: The exact candidate adds effective pre-receive rejection when the configured budget is one and preserves weighted tokenizer-side accounting, but it provisionally charges every unparsed request as one item. Consequently, a budget intended for one N-item request can admit N large N-item bodies concurrently before parsing discovers their true weights. This is a partial fix, not a full resolution of the original weighted pre-scheduler CPU-memory contract.

tests.command: on base: inspect checked-out http_server/admission imports and run 32 concurrent approximately 4 MiB JSON bodies through the actual sglang.srt.entrypoints.http_server.ORJSONRequest.json path
tests.what_was_measured: The prepared base has no MultimodalBodyAdmissionMiddleware or admission module; its actual ORJSONRequest parser accepted and retained all 32 bodies: 134217120 encoded bytes and at least 134216704 decoded-string bytes. Raw logs: /job/review-evidence-j-369ce08d0c96/base-import-and-contract.log and base-actual-orjson-body.log

Candidate regression and controller tests: 11 passed, including the budget-one case where 31 of 32 requests are rejected before receive and lease resize/accounting cases. Raw log: /job/review-evidence-j-369ce08d0c96/candidate-focused-tests.log

tests.command: independent ASGI weighted adversarial case on exact candidate: budget=4, four concurrent 4 MiB bodies, simulated eventual weight=4 each
tests.what_was_measured: All four bodies reached receive concurrently and retained 16777216 bytes while provisional accounting reported only four items; a correctly weighted body-stage limit would admit one such request. Raw log: /job/review-evidence-j-369ce08d0c96/candidate-weighted-adversarial.log

http_server.py and multimodal_preprocessing_admission.py imported from /job/repo/python/sglang; Torch was 2.11.0+rocm7.2 with HIP 7.2. Raw log: /job/review-evidence-j-369ce08d0c96/candidate-import-paths.log

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and candidate change are CPU/ASGI request-body admission logic; no GPU numerical claim was made or needed. The exact Kimi-K2.6 weights and equivalent 1.5 TiB/200-client host workload were unavailable.

native_rebuild_reason: The candidate changes Python, tests, and reports only; no C++, CUDA, HIP, Rust, or other native source changed, and repository-environment.json provides no native rebuild target.
remaining_counterexamples: Before JSON parsing, each request is charged one provisional item regardless of its eventual media count. With budget N, N concurrent bodies can be buffered even when each body later proves to contain N media items and weighted admission should allow only one.

The independent budget=4 adversarial case retained four 4 MiB request bodies (16 MiB total) before true weights were known; all four entered downstream receive under a budget that should fit only one four-item request.

The exact reported 200-client, 28-images/request Kimi-K2.6 failure on a 1.5 TiB host was not reproduced because the model weights and equivalent host were unavailable, so end-to-end prevention remains unverified.
The option is explicitly rejected for SGLANG_RUST_SERVER and EPD language-only mode, so those architectures remain unsupported.
remaining_limitations: Candidate regression coverage proves the special budget-one case, not bounded memory proportional to eventual multimodal item weight during HTTP body receipt.

No model-level semantic, distributed, or Kimi-K2.6 execution was performed; the deterministic tiny Llama fixture would only qualify transport/engine execution and cannot substitute for that architecture or workload.
ASGI-level tests do not quantify socket/kernel/protocol-server buffering outside application receive.
